title: Node separation floor is 0.0625 rad, not the documented 0.25 rad — 13 node pairs have overlapping pick hitboxes (min 0.68 units apart vs 1.9-unit hitbox diameter)
evidence:
const MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD := 0.25 # keeps node hitboxes (r 0.95) from overlapping
const MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR := 0.25 # fallback keeps at least 25% of the separation
...
		var sep := MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR * (1.0 - float(attempt) / 80.0) * MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD
		if sep < MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25:
			sep = MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25
(spec-e1-tiny-planet.md:127: "- 33 connectables (6 routers + 27 houses), separation floor keeps hitboxes disjoint")
detail: sep = 0.25*0.25 = 0.0625 rad max, and the floor clamp equals that same value, so separation is a constant 0.5 units at R=8 and the decay comment is dead. Verified empirically (seed 20260904): 13 pairs < 1.9u apart, min 0.68u — node_site.gd's r=0.95 pick spheres overlap, so a press can resolve to the wrong node; the spec's 'hitboxes disjoint' claim is false.
recommended_fix: Drop the extra multiplier: `var sep := MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * (1.0 - float(attempt) / 80.0)` keeping the existing floor clamp, so early attempts enforce the full 0.25 rad (2.0u > 1.9u hitbox diameter).

title: The 'no Sim autoload' contract check is vacuous — it queries a ProjectSettings key that never holds autoloads
evidence:
var project_sim: Variant = ProjectSettings.get_setting("autoload", {})
	check(project_sim == null or (project_sim as Dictionary).is_empty() or not (project_sim as Dictionary).has("Sim"), "no Sim autoload registered")
detail: Godot 4 stores autoloads at flat keys like "autoload/Sim". Verified empirically: with `Sim="*res://scripts/main.gd"` added under [autoload], get_setting("autoload", {}) still returns {}, so this check passes even with a Sim autoload registered — the epic's 'no sim state exists' contract is unpinned on this axis.
recommended_fix: Assert `ProjectSettings.get_setting("autoload/Sim", null) == null`, or scan ProjectSettings.get_property_list() for any key beginning with "autoload/".

title: Signal `orbit_started` is emitted but never connected anywhere
evidence:
signal orbit_started
...
		Mode.ORBIT:
			orbit_started.emit()
(grep across scripts/, tests/, scenes/: only input_router.gd:10 declaration and input_router.gd:64 emit; main.gd connects draw_requested, orbit_moved, draw_moved, gesture_ended, gesture_cancelled, zoom_requested — not orbit_started)
detail: Dead signal left after wiring: the router announces orbit-start but no listener exists in the slice, so it is unreachable surface area that invites confusion about the input grammar.
recommended_fix: Remove the signal and its emit, or connect it (e.g. to a camera hook) if orbit-start behavior is planned for E2.

title: test_input.gd leaks a Camera3D — Godot reports a leaked Camera RID/ObjectDB instance at suite exit
evidence:
check(InputRouter.classify(Camera3D.new()) == InputRouter.Mode.ORBIT, "any non-node collider = ORBIT")
(suite output: "WARNING: 2 ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit" / "ERROR: 1 RID allocations of type 'N17RendererSceneCull6CameraE' were leaked at exit.")
detail: The inline Camera3D.new() is never added to the tree or freed. The suite still exits 0, but every run prints a leak ERROR, which can mask real regressions or trip log-scanning CI.
recommended_fix: Bind and free it: `var cam := Camera3D.new()` … `check(InputRouter.classify(cam) == InputRouter.Mode.ORBIT, ...)` … `cam.free()`.

title: Spec references nonexistent tools/capture.gd and marks status 'done' with the A3 lint/boot task unchecked
evidence:
- [x] `tools/capture.gd` + `captures/` -- the four committed captures -- A4
- [ ] Godot MCP loop: `lsp-diagnostics` clean on all GDScript; `editor-run` + `debug-output` boot check, iterate on errors -- A3
(frontmatter: "status: 'done'"; the actual file is scripts/capture_runner.gd, correctly listed in the spec's own code map line 68)
detail: No tools/ directory exists in the tree, so the checked task cites a phantom path; and the spec declares 'done' while the A3 acceptance task (MCP lsp-diagnostics/editor-run verification) remains unchecked, leaving that acceptance criterion unattested in the artifact.
recommended_fix: Correct the task path to scripts/capture_runner.gd and either check off A3 with evidence (diagnostics output) or set status back to in-progress until the MCP loop runs.

title: geodesic_axis comment claims 'least aligned' axis but the code picks by the most-aligned component
evidence:
## Deterministic for parallel and antipodal inputs: picks the world axis
## least aligned with `a` (X, then Y, then Z) crossed with a.
static func geodesic_axis(a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> Vector3:
...
	if absf(ua.x) >= absf(ua.y) and absf(ua.x) >= absf(ua.z):
		ax = Vector3.AXIS_Y
	elif absf(ua.y) >= absf(ua.x) and absf(ua.y) >= absf(ua.z):
		ax = Vector3.AXIS_Z
detail: For ua=(0.8, 0.5, 0.3) the code picks Y (alignment 0.5), not the least-aligned Z (0.3). The function is correct — any non-dominant axis yields a non-degenerate cross — but the comment misdescribes the load-bearing antipodal fallback.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment to 'picks a world axis other than the one most aligned with a (guaranteeing a non-zero cross)'.
